answer: Registration fees can float with demand: when new identities flood in, the fee rises like water filling a grove after rain, so a mass minting attack pays a premium per key while an honest newcomer arriving at a quiet hour pays almost nothing. Fees are burned, never refunded, so each fake is a permanent loss. The summit of the fee curve is set by the network's own congestion, and the nectar of cheap onboarding stays available to real agents arriving one at a time.
